config.title: Undo/Redo

intro.title: Undo/Redo
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple text editor with undo and redo functionality. You'll learn how to manage state changes over time using arrays to store history. The main technologies involved are React's useState hook for state management and event handlers for user interactions. By the end, you'll understand how to implement a basic undo/redo system that tracks and navigates through previous states.
intro.usecase: The undo/redo pattern is essential in any interactive application where users can make changes they might want to reverse or reapply. You'll see this in text editors like Google Docs for editing text, in design tools like Figma for adjusting visual elements, and in complex form-based dashboards where users modify filters or data entries. As a developer, implementing this feature prevents user frustration by giving them control over their actions, enhancing the overall usability and professionalism of your application.

objectives: Implement a state management system to track changes in a React component
Construct functions to handle undo and redo operations
Bind user interface controls to the undo and redo functionality
Manipulate component state to restore previous values during undo/redo
Initialize and maintain a history stack for tracking state changes
Render visual feedback indicating undo/redo availability
Integrate keyboard shortcuts for undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y) operations

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The component should return an empty fragment using <> and </>.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: App component is created and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named App and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that it's named App and returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state for current value
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create a state variable named 'value' and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value 0 and destructure the returned array into 'value' and 'setValue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with a number
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'value' that starts at 0, ready to track the current value for the undo/redo functionality.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with initial value 0, and the destructured array includes 'value' and 'setValue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with 0 as the initial value and destructuring the array into 'value' and 'setValue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: call useState(0) inside the component and destructure the returned array.

steps.title: Define handler to update value
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a function named 'updateValue' that takes a parameter 'newValue'. Inside the function, update the 'value' state with the new value, add the new value to the 'history' array, and update the 'historyIndex' to point to the new last position in history.
steps.hint: Remember to use the setter functions for your state variables: setValue, setHistory, and setHistoryIndex. When updating history, you can create a new array that includes all previous history items plus the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an updateValue function that properly updates the current value and maintains the history array with the new value, advancing the history index.
successCriteria: The updateValue function is defined, takes a newValue parameter, updates the value state, adds the new value to history, and updates historyIndex to the new last index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the updateValue function, but it's missing some required logic. Make sure it updates all three state variables: value, history, and historyIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateValue function is not properly defined or doesn't update the state variables correctly. Review the instructions and try again.

steps.title: Define undo handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'handleUndo' inside your component that moves backward in history when possible. The function should check if there's a previous state in history, decrement the history index, and update the current value from history.
steps.hint: Check if historyIndex is greater than 0, then decrement it and set the value from the history array at the new index.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleUndo is defined inside the component that properly implements undo logic.
successCriteria: The handleUndo function exists, checks if undo is possible, decrements historyIndex, and updates value from the history array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the undo handler, but make sure it checks if undo is possible and updates both the history index and current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The undo handler isn't quite right. Remember to check if historyIndex > 0, decrement it, and set the value from history at the new index.

steps.title: Define redo handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'handleRedo' that increments the 'historyIndex' if there are future states in the history,
steps.hint: Check if historyIndex is less than history.length - 1 before incrementing. Then use setHistoryIndex and setValue with the updated index and corresponding history value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleRedo function that safely moves forward in the history array and updates the current value.
successCriteria: The handleRedo function is defined, checks if redo is possible, increments historyIndex, and updates value from the history array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the redo handler, but make sure it checks if redo is possible (historyIndex < history.length - 1) and updates both historyIndex and value correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The redo handler isn't quite right. Remember to check if there are future states before incrementing the index, then update both the index and the current value.

steps.title: Add increment and decrement buttons with onClick handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, add two buttons: one with label 'Increment' that calls updateValue with a higher number, and one with label 'Decrement' that calls updateValue with a lower number. Use onClick handlers to call updateValue with appropriate values.
steps.hint: Create two <button> elements. For the increment button, you might call updateValue(value + 1). For decrement, call updateValue(value - 1).
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the UI: one labeled 'Increment' and one labeled 'Decrement', both wired to call the updateValue function with appropriate values.
successCriteria: Two <button> elements are added inside the return statement, each with onClick handlers that call updateValue with appropriate values (e.g., value + 1 for increment, value - 1 for decrement).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have both increment and decrement buttons, and that they properly call updateValue with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly set up. Check that you have two buttons with onClick handlers that call updateValue with appropriate values.

steps.title: Add undo and redo buttons with onClick handlers
steps.instruction: Add two buttons to your component: one for undo and one for redo. Wire their onClick handlers to the existing handleUndo and handleRedo functions respectively, and add disabled attributes to each button based on whether undo or redo is possible (historyIndex > 0 for undo, historyIndex < history.length - 1 for redo).
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the increment/decrement buttons. Use the existing handleUndo and handleRedo functions for onClick. The disabled attribute should be a boolean expression.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two new buttons appear in the UI: 'Undo' and 'Redo'. They are wired to the correct handlers and become disabled when there's no history to undo/redo.
successCriteria: The component includes an 'Undo' button with onClick={handleUndo} and disabled={historyIndex <= 0}, and a 'Redo' button with onClick={handleRedo} and disabled={historyIndex >= history.length - 1}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the buttons, but check the disabled conditions or onClick handlers. The undo button should be disabled when historyIndex is 0 or less, and redo when historyIndex is at the end of history.
steps.feedbackWrong: The undo and redo buttons are missing or incorrectly implemented. Make sure to add both buttons with onClick handlers and disabled attributes based on historyIndex and history length.
